summary: Adds user search, a per-key request counter and an upstream status check to the directory API, and registers the three routes in main.

findings.title: Search query built from request input
findings.problem: Search pastes the name query parameter straight into the SQL text with Sprintf. Quotes in name are not escaped.
findings.consequence: Any caller of GET /users can inject SQL and read or change any row in the database.
findings.fix: Pass name to QueryContext as a bound parameter instead of formatting it into the query.
findings.suggested_change: rows, err := h.DB.QueryContext(r.Context(), "SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE name = ?", name)

findings.title: Mutex left locked on missing key
findings.problem: Count locks h.mu and then returns early when key is empty without unlocking it.
findings.consequence: One request to GET /count without a key blocks every later Count request forever.
findings.fix: Check key before taking the lock, or unlock with defer right after Lock.

findings.title: Response body closed before error check
findings.problem: fetchStatus defers resp.Body.Close before it checks err. When http.Get fails, resp is nil.
findings.consequence: An unreachable upstream makes the deferred Close panic with a nil pointer. The server then drops the GET /upstream request instead of answering 502.
findings.fix: Move the deferred Close below the err check.

findings.title: New handlers have no tests
findings.problem: The change adds Search, Count and Upstream, and the repository has no test files.
findings.consequence: Bugs like the stuck lock and the nil body panic reached review because no test runs these paths.
findings.fix: Add httptest cases that cover each handler, including its error paths.

dropped.reason: This hit is the same SQL injection on the same line that the c1 finding already covers.
